# ASSET PURCHASE AGREEMENT

This ASSET PURCHASE AGREEMENT (this "**Agreement**") is entered into as of March 2, 2026 by and between **Saitouth Dental Partners, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Buyer**"), and **Trolind Family Dental, P.A.**, a Delaware professional association ("**Seller**"). Buyer and Seller are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Seller owns and operates four dental clinics in New Castle County, Delaware, through which it conducts the Business.

B. Seller wishes to sell to Buyer, and Buyer wishes to purchase from Seller, substantially all of the assets used in the Business, and Buyer will assume certain specified liabilities, on the terms and subject to the conditions of this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants set forth in this Agreement, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

## ARTICLE I. DEFINITIONS

**1.1 Defined Terms.** The following terms have the meanings set forth below:

"**Ancillary Agreements**" means the Seller Note, the IP Assignment, the Bill of Sale, the Assignment and Assumption Agreement, the Transition Services Agreement and each other agreement, instrument and certificate delivered under this Agreement.

"**Assumed Liabilities**" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.4.

"**Business**" means general dentistry, hygiene and orthodontic services conducted at the Clinics.

"**Clinics**" means the dental clinics operated by Seller at (a) 1408 Pennsylvania Avenue, Wilmington, Delaware; (b) 220 East Main Street, Newark, Delaware; (c) 615 North Broad Street, Middletown, Delaware; and (d) 1120 Pulaski Highway, Bear, Delaware.

"**Closing**" and "**Closing Date**" have the meanings set forth in Section 3.1.

"**Fundamental Representations**" means the representations and warranties of Seller in Section 4.1 (Organization and Good Standing), Section 4.2 (Authority; Enforceability), Section 4.5 (Title to Purchased Assets), Section 4.9 (Intellectual Property) and Section 4.14 (Brokers).

"**Governmental Authority**" means any federal, state or local government, regulatory or administrative agency, commission or court, including the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, the Delaware Division of Medicaid and Medical Assistance and the Delaware Board of Dentistry and Dental Hygiene.

"**Intellectual Property Assets**" means all trademarks, service marks, trade names, logos, domain names, social media accounts, copyrights, software (including Seller's patient-recall and appointment-reminder software), databases and other intellectual property owned by Seller and used in the Business, including the items listed on Schedule 4.9.

"**IP Assignment**" means the intellectual property assignment agreement between Seller, as assignor, and Buyer, as assignee, in respect of the Intellectual Property Assets.

"**Losses**" means losses, damages, liabilities, deficiencies, judgments, interest, awards, recoupments, overpayment refunds, penalties, fines, costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees.

"**Payer**" means any Governmental Authority health program (including Medicaid and the Delaware Children's Health Insurance Program), any dental benefits plan and any private insurer or third-party administrator that reimburses dental services.

"**Purchase Price**" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.1.

"**Seller Note**" means the subordinated promissory note issued by Buyer to Seller under Section 2.2(b).

"**Transferred Employees**" means each employee of Seller who accepts Buyer's offer of employment under Section 6.3 and commences employment with Buyer.

"**Transferred Employee Liabilities**" means all liabilities and obligations to or in respect of the Transferred Employees, whether arising before or after the Closing, including accrued and unused paid time off, wage and hour claims, bonus and commission obligations, benefit plan obligations and professional liability (malpractice) tail coverage and related exposure.

**1.2 Interpretation.** Headings are for convenience only. "Including" means "including without limitation." References to Articles, Sections and Schedules are to those of this Agreement unless otherwise stated.

## ARTICLE II. PURCHASE AND SALE

**2.1 Purchase Price.** The aggregate purchase price for the Purchased Assets is $8,400,000 (the "**Purchase Price**"), plus the assumption of the Assumed Liabilities.

**2.2 Payment of the Purchase Price.** Buyer shall pay the Purchase Price as follows:

(a) $6,600,000 at the Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Seller in writing; and

(b) $1,800,000 by delivery at the Closing of the Seller Note, in the principal amount of $1,800,000, payable on the terms set forth therein.

**2.3 Purchased Assets.** At the Closing, Seller shall sell, assign, transfer and deliver to Buyer, and Buyer shall purchase, free and clear of all liens other than permitted liens, all of Seller's right, title and interest in the assets used in the Business (the "**Purchased Assets**"), including: (a) dental chairs, imaging equipment, sterilization equipment, orthodontic equipment, furniture and other tangible personal property located at the Clinics; (b) supplies and inventory; (c) the real property leases for the Clinics listed on Schedule 2.3(c); (d) the contracts listed on Schedule 2.3(d); (e) the Intellectual Property Assets; (f) patient records, charts and radiographs, to the extent transferable under applicable law; (g) telephone numbers and listings; and (h) goodwill of the Business.

**2.4 Assumed Liabilities.** At the Closing, Buyer shall assume only (a) liabilities under the assigned contracts and leases arising after the Closing, and (b) the Transferred Employee Liabilities (together, the "**Assumed Liabilities**").

**2.5 Excluded Liabilities.** Other than the Assumed Liabilities, Buyer does not as

saitouth_trolind_asset_purchase_agreement.md, page 2 of 4:
sume any liability of Seller, including any liability arising from Seller's billing, coding or claims submission to any Payer for services rendered before the Closing.

**2.6 Allocation.** The Purchase Price shall be allocated among the Purchased Assets in accordance with Schedule 2.6 and Section 1060 of the Internal Revenue Code.

## ARTICLE III. CLOSING

**3.1 Closing.** The closing of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the "**Closing**") shall take place remotely by electronic exchange of documents and signatures on March 2, 2026 (the "**Closing Date**"), effective as of 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on the Closing Date.

**3.2 Seller Closing Deliveries.** At the Closing, Seller shall deliver to Buyer: (a) a bill of sale; (b) an assignment and assumption agreement; (c) assignments of the Clinic leases with landlord consents; (d) the Transition Services Agreement; (e) a certificate of good standing of Seller; and (f) a certificate of the Secretary of Seller certifying resolutions authorizing this Agreement.

**3.3 Buyer Closing Deliveries.** At the Closing, Buyer shall deliver to Seller: (a) the cash portion of the Purchase Price under Section 2.2(a); (b) the executed Seller Note; (c) the assignment and assumption agreement; and (d) a certificate of the Secretary of Buyer certifying resolutions authorizing this Agreement.

## ARTICLE IV. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF SELLER

Seller represents and warrants to Buyer as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as follows:

**4.1 Organization and Good Standing.** Seller is a professional association duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware.

**4.2 Authority; Enforceability.** Seller has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement and the Ancillary Agreements and to perform its obligations thereunder. This Agreement constitutes a legal, valid and binding obligation of Seller, enforceable in accordance with its terms.

**4.3 No Conflicts; Consents.** The execution and performance of this Agreement by Seller do not violate Seller's organizational documents, any applicable law or any material contract, except as set forth on Schedule 4.3.

**4.4 Financial Statements.** The financial statements of the Business for the fiscal years ended December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2025 delivered to Buyer were prepared in accordance with GAAP consistently applied and fairly present in all material respects the financial condition and results of operations of the Business.

**4.5 Title to Purchased Assets.** Seller has good and valid title to all Purchased Assets, free and clear of all liens other than permitted liens.

**4.6 Condition of Assets.** The tangible Purchased Assets are in good operating condition and repair, ordinary wear and tear excepted, and are adequate for the uses to which they are being put.

**4.7 Real Property.** Schedule 4.7 lists each lease for the Clinics. Each such lease is in full force and effect, and Seller is not in material default thereunder.

**4.8 Material Contracts.** Schedule 4.8 lists all material contracts of the Business, including all Payer participation agreements. Each is valid and binding, and neither Seller nor, to Seller's knowledge, any counterparty is in material breach.

**4.9 Intellectual Property.** Schedule 4.9 lists all registered and material unregistered Intellectual Property Assets. Seller is the sole and exclusive owner of all Intellectual Property Assets, free and clear of all liens, and has the right to transfer them to Buyer. To Seller's knowledge, the conduct of the Business does not infringe the intellectual property rights of any person, and no person is infringing any Intellectual Property Asset.

**4.10 Litigation.** Except as set forth on Schedule 4.10, there is no action, audit or investigation pending or, to Seller's knowledge, threatened against Seller relating to the Business or the Purchased Assets.

**4.11 Licenses and Permits.** Seller and each dentist and hygienist practicing at the Clinics hold all licenses, permits and registrations (including DEA registrations and radiation equipment registrations) required to conduct the Business as currently conducted.

**4.12 Healthcare Billing and Payer Compliance.** For the six years preceding the Closing Date: (a) all claims submitted by or on behalf of Seller to any Payer were accurate and complete in all material respects, used correct procedure codes, and were supported by appropriate clinical documentation; (b) Seller has complied in all material respects with all Payer participation requirements, the federal Anti-Kickback Statute, the federal False Claims Act, the Delaware Medicaid program rules and all other applicable healthcare laws; (c) Seller has not received any notice of audit, recoupment, overpayment demand or exclusion from any Payer or Governmental Authority, except as set forth on Schedule 4.12; and (d) no credit balances or known overpayments are owed by Seller to any Payer.

**4.13 Employees and Benefit Plans.** Schedule 4.13 lists each employee of Seller with title, compensation, accrued paid time off and date of hire. Seller has complied in all material respects with all applicable employment laws.

**4.14 Brokers.** No broker, finder or investment banker is entitled to any fee in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement based on arrangements made by Seller.

## ARTICLE V. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF BUYER

Buyer represents and warrants to Seller as follows:

**5.1 Organization.** Buyer is a limited liability company duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware.

**5.2 Authority.** Buyer has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement and the Ancillary Agreements, and this Agreement constitutes a legal, valid and binding obligation of Buyer.

**5.3 Sufficiency of Funds.** Buyer has sufficient cash on hand to pay the cash portion of the Purchase Pr

ice at the Closing.

**5.4 Brokers.** No broker, finder or investment banker is entitled to any fee in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement based on arrangements made by Buyer.

## ARTICLE VI. COVENANTS

**6.1 Confidentiality.** From and after the Closing, Seller shall hold in confidence all confidential information concerning the Business and the Purchased Assets.

**6.2 Non-Competition; Non-Solicitation.** For five years after the Closing Date, Seller shall not, directly or indirectly, own, operate or provide dental services through any dental practice located within ten miles of any Clinic, or solicit any Transferred Employee or any patient of the Clinics.

**6.3 Employees.** Buyer shall offer employment, effective as of the Closing, to each employee of Seller listed on Schedule 6.3 on terms substantially comparable in the aggregate to those in effect immediately before the Closing.

**6.4 Patient Records.** Seller and Buyer shall comply with applicable law, including HIPAA and the Delaware dental records regulations, in the transfer and custody of patient records, and Buyer shall provide Seller reasonable access to such records as required for Seller's defense of any audit or claim.

**6.5 Payer Transition.** Following the Closing, Seller shall cooperate with Buyer in Buyer's enrollment with each Payer and shall promptly remit to Buyer any payment received by Seller for services rendered by Buyer after the Closing.

**6.6 Further Assurances; IP Assignment.** Following the Closing, each Party shall execute and deliver such additional instruments as the other Party reasonably requests to give effect to the transactions contemplated by this Agreement. Without limiting the foregoing, Seller shall execute and deliver the IP Assignment and such short-form recordable assignments as are necessary to record the transfer of the Intellectual Property Assets with the United States Patent and Trademark Office and any domain name registrar.

## ARTICLE VII. CONDITIONS TO CLOSING

**7.1 Conditions to Obligations of Buyer.** Buyer's obligation to close is subject to: (a) the accuracy in all material respects of Seller's representations and warranties; (b) Seller's performance in all material respects of its covenants; (c) receipt of the landlord consents listed on Schedule 4.3; and (d) delivery of the items in Section 3.2.

**7.2 Conditions to Obligations of Seller.** Seller's obligation to close is subject to: (a) the accuracy in all material respects of Buyer's representations and warranties; (b) Buyer's performance in all material respects of its covenants; and (c) delivery of the items in Section 3.3.

## ARTICLE VIII. TAX MATTERS

**8.1 Transfer Taxes.** All transfer, sales, use and similar taxes arising from the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be borne equally by Buyer and Seller.

**8.2 Pre-Closing Taxes.** Seller shall be responsible for all taxes relating to the Business or the Purchased Assets for periods ending on or before the Closing Date.

## ARTICLE IX. SURVIVAL; INDEMNIFICATION

**9.1 Survival.** The representations and warranties of Seller contained in this Agreement, including the representations and warranties in Section 4.12, shall survive the Closing until the date that is six (6) months following the Closing Date; provided, that the Fundamental Representations shall survive until sixty (60) days after the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. The representations and warranties of Buyer shall survive the Closing until the date that is six (6) months following the Closing Date. Covenants shall survive in accordance with their terms. No claim may be made in respect of any representation or warranty after its survival period expires, unless a valid Claim Notice was delivered under Section 9.4 before that expiration.

**9.2 Indemnification by Seller.** From and after the Closing, Seller shall indemnify and hold harmless Buyer and its affiliates, officers, managers and employees from and against all Losses arising out of or resulting from:

(a) any inaccuracy in or breach of any representation or warranty of Seller in this Agreement;

(b) any breach of any covenant of Seller in this Agreement; and

(c) any Excluded Liability.

**9.3 Indemnification by Buyer.** From and after the Closing, Buyer shall indemnify and hold harmless Seller and its affiliates, officers, directors and employees from and against all Losses arising out of or resulting from:

(a) any inaccuracy in or breach of any representation or warranty of Buyer in this Agreement;

(b) the Transferred Employee Liabilities; and

(c) any breach of any covenant of Buyer in this Agreement or any other Assumed Liability.

**9.4 Indemnification Procedures.**

(a) *Notice.* A Party seeking indemnification (the "**Indemnified Party**") shall deliver written notice of its claim (a "**Claim Notice**") to the Party from which indemnification is sought (the "**Indemnifying Party**").

(b) *Contents of Claim Notice.* A Claim Notice shall describe in reasonable detail the facts giving rise to the claim and the provision of this Agreement under which indemnification is sought, and shall include invoices, remittance records or other documentation of Losses actually paid by the Indemnified Party. A Claim Notice that does not satisfy this Section 9.4(b) shall not be valid.

(c) *Third-Party Claims.* The Indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any third-party claim with counsel reasonably acceptable to the Indemnified Party by notice given within thirty days after receipt of the Claim Notice. The Indemnified Party may participate in the defense at its own cost. Neither Party shall settle a third-party claim without the other Party's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

(d) *Payment.* The Indemnifying Party shall pay any undisputed amount within thirty days after receipt of a valid Claim Notice. Disputed amounts shall be resolved under Section 11.7.

**9.5 Limitations.**

a) *Cap.* Seller's aggregate liability under Section 9.2(a) shall not exceed 10% of the Purchase Price ($840,000) (the "**Cap**").

(b) *Fundamental Representations and Fraud.* The Cap shall not apply to Losses arising out of any inaccuracy in or breach of the Fundamental Representations, including Section 4.9, or to fraud. Seller's aggregate liability for such Losses, other than in the case of fraud, shall not exceed the Purchase Price.

(c) *Buyer Cap.* Buyer's aggregate liability under Section 9.3, other than Section 9.3(b), shall not exceed the Cap.

(d) *Basket.* Seller shall not be liable under Section 9.2(a), other than for breach of the Fundamental Representations, until the aggregate Losses exceed $84,000, after which Seller shall be liable only for Losses in excess of that amount.

(e) *Insurance.* Losses shall be calculated net of insurance proceeds actually received by the Indemnified Party.

(f) *Mitigation.* Each Indemnified Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate Losses.

**9.6 Set-off.** Buyer may set off amounts owed to it under this Article IX against amounts payable under the Seller Note solely in accordance with the terms of the Seller Note.

**9.7 Exclusive Remedy.** Except for fraud, claims for specific performance or injunctive relief, and claims under the Ancillary Agreements, the indemnification provided in this Article IX is the sole and exclusive remedy of the Parties for any breach of this Agreement.

**9.8 Tax Treatment.** Indemnification payments shall be treated as adjustments to the Purchase Price for tax purposes unless otherwise required by law.

## ARTICLE X. TERMINATION

**10.1 Termination.** This Agreement may be terminated before the Closing (a) by mutual written consent; (b) by either Party if the Closing has not occurred by March 31, 2026, unless caused by the terminating Party's breach; or (c) by either Party upon a material uncured breach by the other Party.

**10.2 Effect of Termination.** Upon termination, this Agreement shall be of no further force or effect, except Section 6.1, this Section 10.2 and Article XI, and except that no Party is relieved of liability for willful breach.

## ARTICLE XI. MISCELLANEOUS

**11.1 Expenses.** Except as otherwise provided, each Party shall bear its own costs and expenses in connection with this Agreement.

**11.2 Notices.** All notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, nationally recognized overnight courier or email with confirmation of transmission, to the addresses set forth on the signature page or such other address as a Party designates by notice.

**11.3 Severability.** If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect.

**11.4 Amendment and Waiver.** This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both Parties. No waiver is effective unless in writing and signed by the waiving Party.

**11.5 Assignment.** Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party, except that Buyer may assign its rights to an affiliate or collaterally to its lenders.

**11.6 Governing Law.** This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

**11.7 Jurisdiction; Waiver of Jury Trial.** Each Party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (or, if that court lacks jurisdiction, the Superior Court of the State of Delaware or the United States District Court for the District of Delaware). EACH PARTY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT.

**11.8 Order of Precedence.** In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and any Ancillary Agreement, this Agreement shall control, except that the IP Assignment shall control as to the Assigned IP (as defined in the IP Assignment).

**11.9 Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument.

# CONFIRMATORY INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ASSIGNMENT AGREEMENT

This CONFIRMATORY INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ASSIGNMENT AGREEMENT (this "**Assignment**") is entered into as of October 12, 2026 by and between **Trolind Family Dental, P.A.**, a Delaware professional association ("**Assignor**"), and **Saitouth Dental Partners, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Assignee**"). Assignor and Assignee are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Assignor, as Seller, and Assignee, as Buyer, are parties to the Asset Purchase Agreement dated as of March 2, 2026 (the "**Purchase Agreement**"), under which Assignor sold to Assignee substantially all of the assets used in the operation of Assignor's four dental clinics in New Castle County, Delaware.

B. Section 6.6 of the Purchase Agreement requires Assignor to execute and deliver this Assignment and such short-form recordable assignments as are necessary to record the transfer of the intellectual property sold under the Purchase Agreement with the United States Patent and Trademark Office and any domain name registrar.

C. The Parties are entering into this Assignment to confirm and record the transfer of the Assigned IP to Assignee.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants in this Assignment and the Purchase Agreement, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 **Defined Terms.** The following terms have the meanings set forth below:

"**Assigned IP**" means all intellectual property owned by Assignor and used primarily in the Business, including:

(a) the trademarks, service marks, trade names, logos and trade dress listed on Schedule A, together with all common-law rights therein, all registrations and applications for registration thereof, and all goodwill of the Business connected with the use thereof and symbolized thereby (the "**Assigned Marks**");

(b) the domain names and social media accounts listed on Schedule B (the "**Assigned Domains**");

(c) the software listed on Schedule C, including Assignor's patient-recall and appointment-reminder software, in source code and object code form, together with all documentation, configurations, templates and data structures relating thereto (the "**Assigned Software**");

(d) all copyrights in website content, patient education materials, marketing materials, forms and other works of authorship, whether registered or unregistered; and

(e) all databases and compilations, including patient-recall lists, to the extent transferable under applicable law.

"**Business**" means general dentistry and hygiene services conducted at the Clinics.

"**Cap**" has the meaning given in Section 9.5(a) of the Purchase Agreement.

"**Clinics**" has the meaning given in Section 1.1 of the Purchase Agreement.

"**Closing Date**" has the meaning given in Section 3.1 of the Purchase Agreement.

"**Intellectual Property Rights**" means all rights in and to the Assigned IP throughout the world, including all rights to sue for and collect damages and other remedies for past, present and future infringement, dilution, misappropriation or other violation, and all income, royalties and payments now or hereafter due with respect to the Assigned IP.

1.2 **Other Terms.** Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Assignment have the meanings given in the Purchase Agreement.

## 2. ASSIGNMENT

2.1 **Assignment.** Assignor hereby irrevocably sells, assigns, transfers, conveys and delivers to Assignee, and confirms its prior sale, assignment, transfer and conveyance to Assignee effective as of the Closing Date, all of Assignor's right, title and interest in and to the Assigned IP and the Intellectual Property Rights, free and clear of all liens.

2.2 **Acceptance.** Assignee hereby accepts the assignment of the Assigned IP and the Intellectual Property Rights.

2.3 **Goodwill.** The assignment of the Assigned Marks includes the goodwill of the Business connected with the use of and symbolized by the Assigned Marks, and Assignor shall not use any Assigned Mark or any mark confusingly similar thereto after the date of this Assignment.

2.4 **Moral Rights.** To the extent permitted by applicable law, Assignor waives, and shall cause its employees and contractors who authored any Assigned IP to waive, all moral rights in the Assigned IP.

## 3. CONSIDERATION

The consideration for the assignment in Section 2 is included in the Purchase Price paid under the Purchase Agreement. No additional consideration is payable by Assignee under this Assignment.

## 4. DELIVERY; RECORDATION

4.1 **Delivery of Software and Materials.** Within ten (10) business days after the date of this Assignment, Assignor shall deliver to Assignee (a) complete copies of the source code and object code of the Assigned Software, together with all build instructions, administrator credentials and license keys, and (b) all files, specimens and correspondence relating to the Assigned Marks, in each case to the extent not previously delivered.

4.2 **Domain Names and Accounts.** Within five (5) business days after the date of this Assignment, Assignor shall take all actions required by the applicable registrar or platform to transfer the registrant and administrative control of each Assigned Domain to Assignee or its designee.

4.3 **Recordation.** Assignor authorizes Assignee to record this Assignment, or a short-form assignment in the form of Exhibit 1, with the United States Patent and Trademark Office, the United States Copyright Office and any other Governmental Authority or registrar. Assignor shall execute any such short-form assignment upon Assignee's request.

## 5. FURTHER ASSURANCES

5.1 **Further Instruments.** Assignor shall, at Assignee's reasonable request and without further consideration, execute and deliver such further instruments and take such further actions as are reasonably necessary

 to vest in Assignee full title to the Assigned IP and to perfect, record or enforce Assignee's rights therein.

5.3 **Cooperation in Enforcement.** Assignor shall reasonably cooperate, at Assignee's expense, in any action brought by Assignee to enforce or defend the Assigned IP, including by providing testimony and documents.

## 6. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

6.1 **Assignor.** Assignor represents and warrants to Assignee that:

(a) Assignor has full power and authority to enter into this Assignment and to perform its obligations hereunder, and this Assignment constitutes a legal, valid and binding obligation of Assignor;

(b) the representations and warranties in Section 4.9 of the Purchase Agreement are true and correct as to the Assigned IP as of the date of this Assignment as though made on that date; and

(c) Assignor has not granted any license, option or other right in the Assigned IP to any person that remains in effect, other than as listed on Schedule 4.9 to the Purchase Agreement.

6.2 **Assignee.** Assignee represents and warrants to Assignor that it has full power and authority to enter into this Assignment, and this Assignment constitutes a legal, valid and binding obligation of Assignee.

## 7. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

Assignor's aggregate liability for any inaccuracy in or breach of its representations and warranties with respect to the Assigned IP, whether under this Assignment or the Purchase Agreement, including Section 4.9 of the Purchase Agreement, shall not exceed the Cap. Claims under this Section 7 shall be made in accordance with the procedures in Section 9.4 of the Purchase Agreement.

## 8. GOVERNING LAW; JURISDICTION

8.1 **Governing Law.** This Assignment shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict of laws principles, except to the extent that the federal laws of the United States govern the assignment of registered trademarks and copyrights.

9.3 **Amendment and Waiver.** This Assignment may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both Parties. No waiver is effective unless in writing and signed by the waiving Party.

9.4 **Severability.** If any provision of this Assignment is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect.

9.5 **Counterparts.** This Assignment may be executed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument.

# SUBORDINATED PROMISSORY NOTE

**$1,800,000**
**Issue Date: March 2, 2026**
**Wilmington, Delaware**

FOR VALUE RECEIVED, **Saitouth Dental Partners, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Maker**"), promises to pay to the order of **Trolind Family Dental, P.A.**, a Delaware professional association ("**Holder**"), the principal amount and interest set out below, on the terms and subject to the conditions of this Subordinated Promissory Note (this "**Note**").

This Note is the Seller Note issued under Section 2.2(b) of the Asset Purchase Agreement dated as of March 2, 2026 between Maker, as Buyer, and Holder, as Seller (the "**Purchase Agreement**"). March 2, 2026 is the "**Issue Date**" of this Note. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Note have the meanings given in the Purchase Agreement.

## 1. PRINCIPAL

1.1 **Principal Amount.** The principal amount of this Note is $1,800,000 (the "**Principal Amount**"). The Principal Amount is part of the Purchase Price.

1.2 **Maturity.** The entire unpaid Principal Amount, with all accrued and unpaid interest, is due and payable on March 2, 2029 (the "**Maturity Date**"), unless paid earlier under this Note.

## 2. INTEREST

2.1 **Rate.** Interest accrues on the unpaid Principal Amount from the Issue Date at a fixed rate of six percent (6%) per year, computed on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed.

2.2 **Default Rate.** While an Event of Default is continuing, interest accrues on the unpaid Principal Amount at a rate of eight percent (8%) per year.

2.3 **Maximum Lawful Rate.** Interest under this Note shall not exceed the maximum rate permitted by applicable law. Any interest paid in excess of that rate shall be applied to reduce the Principal Amount.

## 3. PAYMENTS

3.1 **Installments.** Maker shall pay the Principal Amount in twelve (12) equal quarterly installments of $150,000 each, on the second day of each June, September, December and March, beginning June 2, 2026 and ending on the Maturity Date (each, an "**Installment Date**").

3.2 **Interest Payments.** Maker shall pay accrued interest in arrears on each Installment Date.

3.3 **Manner of Payment.** Maker shall make all payments in lawful money of the United States by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account Holder designates in writing from time to time.

3.4 **Business Days.** If a payment is due on a day that is not a Business Day, it is due on the next Business Day, and interest shall accrue for the additional days. "**Business Day**" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or day on which commercial banks in Wilmington, Delaware are authorized or required to close.

3.5 **Application of Payments.** Payments shall be applied first to costs of collection payable under Section 8.2, then to accrued interest, and then to the Principal Amount in the order of the installments next due.

## 4. PREPAYMENT

Maker may prepay this Note in whole or in part at any time without premium or penalty. Each partial prepayment shall be accompanied by accrued interest on the amount prepaid and shall be applied to the remaining installments in inverse order of maturity.

## 5. SET-OFF

5.1 **Right of Set-off.** Subject to Section 5.2, Maker may set off against any installment of principal or interest under this Note the amount of any Losses for which Maker is entitled to indemnification under Article IX of the Purchase Agreement, as provided in Section 9.6 of the Purchase Agreement.

5.2 **Set-off Notice.** Maker may exercise its right under Section 5.1 only if Maker delivers to Holder a written notice (a "**Set-off Notice**") within one hundred fifty (150) days after the Issue Date. Each Set-off Notice shall state the amount to be set off, identify the installment or installments against which the set-off will be applied, and attach or refer to the Claim Notice delivered under Section 9.4 of the Purchase Agreement in respect of the related Losses.

5.3 **Disputed Amounts.** If Holder disputes an amount stated in a Set-off Notice, Holder shall notify Maker in writing within thirty (30) days after receipt of the Set-off Notice. Maker may withhold the disputed amount until the dispute is resolved by written agreement of Maker and Holder or by a final, non-appealable order of a court of competent jurisdiction under Section 11.7 of the Purchase Agreement. Within ten (10) Business Days after that resolution, Maker shall pay to Holder any withheld amount determined not to be owed to Maker, with interest at the rate in Section 2.1 from the date the amount would otherwise have been due.

5.4 **Effect of Set-off.** Any amount properly set off under this Section 5 reduces the Principal Amount and interest payable under this Note and shall be treated as a payment by Holder of the corresponding indemnification obligation under the Purchase Agreement. Except as provided in this Section 5, Maker's obligation to pay this Note is absolute and unconditional.

## 6. SUBORDINATION

6.1 **Subordination.** The payment of principal and interest under this Note is subordinated in right of payment to the prior payment in full of all Senior Indebtedness. "**Senior Indebtedness**" means all indebtedness of Maker for borrowed money owed to any bank, commercial finance lender or other institutional lender (each, a "**Senior Lender**"), including principal, interest, fees and expenses, whether existing on the Issue Date or incurred later.

6.2 **Permitted Payments.** Unless a payment default or acceleration has occurred and is continuing under the Senior Indebtedness and the Senior Lender has delivered written notice of it to Holder, Maker may make, and Holder may receive, regularly scheduled payments of principal and interest under this Note.

6.3 **Turnover.** Any payment received by Holder in violation of this Section 6 shall be held in trust for the Senior Lender and promptly paid over to it.

6.4 **Subordination Agreement.** Holder shall, on request

## 7. EVENTS OF DEFAULT

Each of the following is an "**Event of Default**":

(a) Maker fails to pay any principal or interest within ten (10) Business Days after the date due, other than an amount withheld under Section 5;

(b) Maker makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, becomes the subject of any voluntary or involuntary proceeding under any bankruptcy, insolvency or similar law that, if involuntary, is not dismissed within sixty (60) days, or admits in writing its inability to pay its debts as they become due; or

(c) Maker sells or otherwise transfers all or substantially all of the Purchased Assets to a person that is not an affiliate of Maker, unless this Note is repaid in full at or before the completion of that transfer.

## 8. REMEDIES

8.1 **Acceleration.** Subject to Section 6, upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, Holder may, by written notice to Maker, declare the entire unpaid Principal Amount and all accrued interest immediately due and payable. Upon an Event of Default under Section 7(b), those amounts become due and payable automatically without notice.

8.2 **Costs of Collection.** Maker shall pay Holder's reasonable attorneys' fees and costs incurred in collecting any amount due and unpaid after an Event of Default.

8.3 **Waivers.** Maker waives presentment, demand, protest, notice of dishonor and all other notices in connection with this Note, except notices expressly required by this Note.

## 9. MISCELLANEOUS

9.1 **Notices.** Notices under this Note shall be given in accordance with Section 11.2 of the Purchase Agreement.

9.2 **Transfer.** Holder may not assign, pledge or transfer this Note without Maker's prior written consent. Maker may not assign its obligations under this Note without Holder's prior written consent, except to an affiliate of Maker that assumes those obligations in writing, in which case Maker remains liable.

9.3 **Amendment and Waiver.** This Note may be amended only by a written instrument signed by Maker and Holder. No waiver is effective unless in writing and signed by the waiving party. No delay in exercising any right under this Note operates as a waiver of that right.

9.4 **Severability.** If any provision of this Note is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force and effect.

9.5 **Governing Law.** This Note is governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

9.6 **Jurisdiction; Waiver of Jury Trial.** Section 11.7 of the Purchase Agreement applies to this Note as if set out in full in it, with references to "this Agreement" read as references to this Note.

9.7 **Lost Note.** If this Note is lost, stolen, destroyed or mutilated, Maker shall issue a replacement note on identical terms after receiving an affidavit of loss and an indemnity reasonably satisfactory to Maker.

9.8 **Counterparts; Electronic Signature.** This Note may be executed and delivered by electronic signature, which is as effective as an original signature.

**Re: Proposed Acquisition of the Assets of Trolind Family Dental, P.A.**

Ladies and Gentlemen:

This letter of intent (this "**Letter**") sets out the principal terms on which Saitouth Dental Partners, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("**Buyer**"), proposes to acquire substantially all of the assets of Trolind Family Dental, P.A., a Delaware professional association ("**Seller**"). The proposed acquisition is referred to in this Letter as the "**Transaction**." Except as stated in Paragraph 14, this Letter is not binding on either party and is intended only as a basis for negotiating a definitive asset purchase agreement (the "**Definitive Agreement**").

## 1. Business and Clinics

Seller currently operates four dental clinics in New Castle County, Delaware. The clinics are located at 1408 Pennsylvania Avenue, Wilmington; 220 East Main Street, Newark; 615 North Broad Street, Middletown; and 1120 Pulaski Highway, Bear (the "**Clinics**"). Through the Clinics, Seller provides general dentistry, hygiene and orthodontic services (the "**Business**"). Buyer's proposal covers the Business as a whole, including the orthodontic practice and its related brands, equipment and patient-recall systems.

## 2. Purchased Assets and Assumed Liabilities

(a) Buyer will acquire, free and clear of all liens other than customary permitted liens, substantially all of Seller's assets used in the Business. These include:

- equipment, including orthodontic equipment, furniture and other tangible personal property;
- supplies and inventory;
- the Clinic leases;
- assigned contracts;
- patient records, to the extent transferable under applicable law;
- telephone numbers;
- goodwill; and
- all intellectual property used in the Business. This includes the TROLIND FAMILY DENTAL and related marks, domain names, social media accounts, and Seller's patient-recall and appointment-reminder software.

(b) Buyer will assume only (i) liabilities under assigned contracts and leases that arise after closing, and (ii) the obligations to transferred employees to be agreed in the Definitive Agreement. All other liabilities remain with Seller. In particular, Seller retains any liability arising from its billing, coding or claims submission to any payer for services rendered before closing.

## 3. Purchase Price

The aggregate purchase price will be $8,400,000 (the "**Purchase Price**"), plus the assumption of the assumed liabilities described in Paragraph 2(b). The Purchase Price is based on the financial statements of the Business for the fiscal years ended December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2025. It assumes the Business is delivered with a customary level of working supplies and no material adverse change before closing.

## 4. Payment of the Purchase Price

The Purchase Price will be paid as follows:

(a) $6,600,000 in cash at closing; and

(b) $1,800,000 by a subordinated promissory note issued by Buyer to Seller at closing (the "**Seller Note**"). The Seller Note will bear interest at a fixed rate of six percent (6%) per year, will be payable in equal quarterly installments over three years, and may be prepaid without premium or penalty. The Seller Note will be subordinated to Buyer's senior institutional indebtedness on customary terms. Buyer will have the right to set off amounts owed to it for indemnifiable losses against payments due under the Seller Note, on terms to be set out in the Definitive Agreement and the Seller Note.

## 5. Representations and Warranties

The Definitive Agreement will contain representations and warranties customary for an acquisition of a dental practice of this size. These will include representations as to:

- organization;
- authority;
- title to assets;
- financial statements;
- condition of assets;
- leases;
- material contracts and payer participation agreements;
- intellectual property;
- litigation;
- licenses and permits (including DEA and radiation equipment registrations);
- employees; and
- brokers.

They will also include a representation on healthcare billing and payer compliance. That representation will cover claims accuracy, coding, clinical documentation and compliance with Medicaid, the Delaware Children's Health Insurance Program, private payer requirements and applicable federal and state healthcare laws, in each case for a six-year lookback period.

## 6. Survival

Seller's representations and warranties will survive for 18 months after closing. This includes the healthcare billing and payer compliance representations. Seller's representations as to organization, authority, title to assets, intellectual property and brokers (the "**Fundamental Representations**") will survive until sixty (60) days after the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. Buyer's representations and warranties will survive for the same general survival period as Seller's.

## 7. Indemnification

(a) Seller will indemnify Buyer for losses arising from:

- breaches of Seller's representations, warranties and covenants; and
- excluded liabilities, including pre-closing payer recoupments, overpayment refunds, penalties and fines.

(b) Seller's liability for breaches of representations and warranties will be capped at 10% of the Purchase Price ($840,000). This cap will not apply to breaches of the Fundamental Representations or to fraud. Seller's liability for breaches of the Fundamental Representations, other than fraud, will be capped at the Purchase Price.

(c) Seller will not be liable for breaches of representations and warranties, other than the Fundamental Representations, until aggregate losses exceed $84,000. After that threshold, Seller will be liable only for the excess.

(d) Buyer will indemnify Seller for

 breaches of Buyer's representations, warranties and covenants and for the assumed liabilities. Buyer's indemnity obligations will be subject to a cap on terms to be agreed in the Definitive Agreement.

(e) The indemnification procedures will be customary. A claim notice will describe the claim in reasonable detail. It may be given for losses that have been incurred or are reasonably anticipated, including losses arising from a pending audit or recoupment demand.

## 8. Employees

Buyer will offer employment, effective at closing, to the dentists, hygienists, orthodontic staff and other employees of Seller identified by Buyer. The offers will be on terms substantially comparable in the aggregate to their current terms. The treatment of accrued paid time off, wage obligations, benefit plan obligations and professional liability tail coverage will be addressed in the Definitive Agreement.

## 9. Restrictive Covenants

For five years after closing, Seller will not, directly or indirectly:

- own, operate or provide dental services through any dental practice within ten miles of any Clinic; or
- solicit any transferred employee or any patient of the Clinics.

## 10. Conditions to Closing

Closing will be subject to the following conditions:

- completion of Buyer's legal, financial, billing and operational due diligence to Buyer's satisfaction;
- negotiation and execution of the Definitive Agreement and related ancillary agreements;
- receipt of landlord consents for the Clinic leases;
- arrangements satisfactory to Buyer for transition of payer enrollment;
- the absence of any material adverse change in the Business; and
- receipt of all required approvals.

## 11. Intellectual Property Transfer

At or after closing, Seller will execute an intellectual property assignment and short-form recordable assignments. These will transfer and record the transfer of all intellectual property used in the Business, including the general dentistry, hygiene and orthodontic brands and the patient-recall software, with the United States Patent and Trademark Office and applicable domain name registrars.

## 12. Timing

The parties will use good faith efforts to execute the Definitive Agreement and close the Transaction on or about March 2, 2026.

## 13. Due Diligence and Access

Seller will give Buyer and its advisors reasonable access to the following, subject to applicable privacy law, including HIPAA:

- the Clinics;
- Seller's books, records, payer agreements, audit correspondence and claims data;
- Seller's employees and professional staff; and
- Seller's software and intellectual property documentation.

## 14. Binding Provisions

Only the following provisions of this Letter are legally binding on the parties: this Paragraph 14 and Paragraphs 15, 16, 17 and 18. No other binding obligation will arise with respect to the Transaction unless and until the Definitive Agreement is executed and delivered. Either party may terminate negotiations at any time before execution of the Definitive Agreement by written notice to the other.

## 15. Exclusivity

From the date Seller countersigns this Letter until the earlier of (a) March 31, 2026 and (b) termination of negotiations under Paragraph 14, Seller will not, directly or indirectly, solicit, negotiate or accept any proposal for the sale of the Business, the Clinics or any material portion of Seller's assets with any person other than Buyer.

## 16. Confidentiality

Each party will keep the terms of this Letter and all information furnished in connection with the Transaction confidential, except as required by law or as disclosed to its advisors and financing sources who are bound by confidentiality obligations.

## 17. Expenses

Each party will bear its own costs and expenses in connection with this Letter and the Transaction.

## 18. Governing Law

This Letter is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

# Saitouth Dental Partners Completes Acquisition of Trolind Family Dental's Four New Castle County Clinics

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**

**WILMINGTON, Delaware, March 3, 2026.** Saitouth Dental Partners, LLC ("Saitouth"), a dental service organization supporting community dental practices in the Mid-Atlantic region, announced today that it has completed its acquisition of substantially all of the assets of Trolind Family Dental, P.A. ("Trolind Family Dental"). Trolind Family Dental operates four general dentistry and orthodontic clinics in New Castle County, Delaware. The transaction closed on March 2, 2026.

## 1. Transaction Overview

Under an asset purchase agreement governed by Delaware law, Saitouth acquired the operations, equipment, clinic leases, patient relationships and goodwill of the four Trolind Family Dental clinics. The clinics provide general dentistry, hygiene and orthodontic services. The acquired clinics are located at:

- 1408 Pennsylvania Avenue, Wilmington, Delaware;
- 220 East Main Street, Newark, Delaware;
- 615 North Broad Street, Middletown, Delaware; and
- 1120 Pulaski Highway, Bear, Delaware.

The parties did not disclose the financial terms of the transaction.

## 2. Continuity of Patient Care

All four clinics remain open and continue to see patients at their current locations and hours. Patients do not need to take any action. Existing appointments, treatment plans and orthodontic treatment in progress will continue as scheduled. Patient records will remain available at each clinic in accordance with applicable privacy law, including HIPAA.

Saitouth offered employment to the dentists, hygienists, orthodontic staff and other team members of the clinics, effective at closing. Patients will continue to be cared for by the clinical teams they know.

## 3. Insurance and Payer Participation

Saitouth is working with Medicaid, the Delaware Children's Health Insurance Program and private dental benefits plans to transition payer enrollment for the clinics. Patients should continue to present their current insurance information at their next visit. Clinic staff will contact patients directly if any change affects their coverage.

## 4. Management Commentary

"Trolind Family Dental has built a strong reputation in New Castle County for family-centered general and orthodontic care," said the Chief Executive Officer of Saitouth Dental Partners. "We are pleased to welcome the Trolind clinical teams. We look forward to supporting them with the operational, technology and administrative resources they need to keep focusing on their patients."

"We chose Saitouth because it shares our commitment to accessible, high-quality care for families in our community," said the President of Trolind Family Dental. "This partnership positions our clinics and our staff for the next chapter of growth."

## 5. About Saitouth Dental Partners, LLC

Saitouth Dental Partners, LLC is a Delaware limited liability company headquartered at 300 Delaware Avenue, Suite 900, Wilmington, Delaware 19801. Saitouth provides non-clinical business support to affiliated dental practices, including:

- billing and revenue cycle management;
- payer enrollment;
- human resources;
- technology; and
- facilities management.

Clinical decisions remain with licensed dental professionals.

## 6. About Trolind Family Dental

Trolind Family Dental has provided general dentistry, hygiene and orthodontic services to patients across New Castle County, Delaware through clinics in Wilmington, Newark, Middletown and Bear.

## 7. Forward-Looking Statements

This press release contains forward-looking statements about the expected benefits of the transaction, the continuity of clinic operations and the transition of payer enrollment. These statements are based on current expectations and involve risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Saitouth undertakes no obligation to update any forward-looking statement except as required by law.
